title: leadership-cohort-weekly-blitz-2027-12-08
content:
Leadership Cohort — Weekly Blitz notes (2027-12-08)
Owners: Asha (chair), Liam, Mariana, Ellen, Diego
Attendees: eng leads from serving-runtime, platform-engineering, private-deployments, observability, product-hosted-api, SRE
Length: 45m (tight cadence)
Purpose: rapid cross-team alignment on hot signals, runway risks, fast blockers, and decisions for next sprint window. Keep actions small and owned.

1) Top signals since last week
- Latency tail increased 7% for 4k token streams in eu-west for the 2.3.x runtime build. Spike coincided with nightly backup window on dedicated pools. (Reported by: serving-runtime SLI alerts).
- Cost per generated token improved by ~12% on internal compute pool after quant profile adjustments, but quality regressions in rare prompt shapes surfaced in internal evals. (Applied ML + Optimize).
- Private-deployments: two customers reported setup failures with KMS key rotation in VPC deployments when using external HSM gateway. Failures started after patch libcrypto update.
- Observability: increased noise from ephemeral transient 429s in the routing layer due to short-lived rate-limit bursts. Need smoother backoff shaping.

2) Quick triage & assignments (10m)
- Latency tail on 2.3.x: immediate mitigation = throttle nightly backups on dedicated pools for 00:00–02:00 UTC in eu regions. Owner: Diego (platform-engineering). Due: 2027-12-09 EOD.
- Root-cause deep-dive: serving-runtime to capture KV cache hit distribution and scheduler logs for impacted intervals. Owner: Liam (serving-runtime infra). Due: 2027-12-10. Linked: GH PR #542 for a scheduler metrics patch.
- Cost/quality regression: revert quant profile in canary until we get targeted eval set for failing prompts. Owner: Mariana (applied-ml). Due: 2027-12-09 morning. Note: run the focused eval harness on the 20 prompt shapes marked in /evals/quant-regress-2027-12.
- KMS rotation failures: Private-deployments team to produce a minimal repro and confirm if libcrypto change is source. Owner: Ellen. Due: 2027-12-11. Temporary workaround: recommend pinning to previous libcrypto version in installer docs.
- Routing 429 noise: SRE to prototype exponential-bump token bucket smoothing and push a config toggle to rollout to prod-canary. Owner: SRE lead (Jonah). Due: 2027-12-10.

3) Decisions made (5m)
- Canary delta threshold for automatic fallback tightened from 15% to 8% request-error-rate for hosted-api. Rationale: observed user-visible regressions during multi-model rollouts. Action: product-hosted-api to update rollout config. Owner: Product infra PM (Priya).
- Dedicated pools will have a new optional slot labeling for "backup-safe" workloads to allow staggered IO heavy jobs. Pilot with two customers next week. Owner: Diego.

4) Cross-team blockers requiring coordination (5m)
- Observability retention policy: recent incident required extended trace retention and the team is hitting retention budget. Platform-engineering must provision an expansion plan or selective retention by trace tags. Blocker for postmortem completeness. Owner: Observability lead (Mariana to coordinate).
- SDK compatibility: dev-ex reported two regressions in streaming chunking behavior for Python SDK that affects function-calling edge-cases. Requires a combined patch across runtime and SDK. Owner: Developer-experience + serving-runtime (Liam + Nora). Target: 2027-12-15.

5) Upcoming rollouts & readiness checklist (8m)
- Runtime 2.3.1 candidate: contains scheduler metrics, small GC changes, and quant profile management. Must pass: canary perf test (latency p99 within 5% of baseline), canary quality smoke (20 eval prompts), and upgrade rollback test. Canary window: 2027-12-12 to 2027-12-14.
- Dedicated autoscale policy feature: enabling burst-buckets for enterprise customers. Need security review of burst telemetry. Owner: Platform security + product-dedicated. Review due 2027-12-13.
- Private on-prem installer revision (v1.9): includes KMS pinning and install-time preflight. Private-deployments to publish upgrade notes and one-click rollback.

6) Risk register snapshot (3m)
- External: HSM gateway compatibility drift — medium risk until libcrypto repro is confirmed.
- Internal: cumulative p99 drift from background maintenance windows — high for eu-west.
- Cost: aggressive quantization rollout can produce unseen edge-case hallucination regressions — medium.

7) Action items (clear owners and due dates)
- Diego: implement backup-safe slot labels + schedule staggering plan. Due 2027-12-13.
- Liam: attach scheduler logs & KV cache histograms to ticket LINKED-2048. Due 2027-12-10.
- Mariana: revert canary quant profile; run targeted evals; produce short summary of failing prompt shapes. Due 2027-12-09.
- Ellen: produce KMS minimal-repro and emergency install note for customers. Due 2027-12-11.
- Jonah (SRE): push 429 smoothing prototype to prod-canary and report early telemetry. Due 2027-12-10.
- Priya: update hosted-api rollout config threshold and communicate to success teams. Due 2027-12-09.
- Nora + Liam: coordinate SDK/runtime patch for streaming chunking. Due 2027-12-15.

8) Parking lot (items we did not have time for)
- Long-term: unified canary dashboard that surfaces quality deltas by prompt bucket (priority Q1).
- Investigate improved preflight for private installs to catch lib dep mismatches earlier.
- Rollout of per-route economic telemetry to better attribute cost to model-decisions.

9) Quick wins for next sync (two bullets)
- Ship a lite backoff patch in routing config to reduce 429 noise for low-priority routes.
- Publish a short "quant rollback playbook" so product + solutions can respond quickly to customer reports.

Minutes taken by: Asha Patel
Notes: keep this doc as the single source for actions; please add updates inline with date stamps. If you are an owner, append status: in_progress|blocked|done and short link to progress.

Conversation snippets (informal):
- Liam: "I think the scheduler issue shows up when KV hit rate drops below 65% and the batcher starts thrashing."
- Mariana: "We need to be surgical with quant rollouts — broad rollback is cheaper than chasing subtle model-quality issues in prod."
- Ellen: "Pinning libcrypto is ugly but buys time to test the HSM gateway against the new patch."

Attachments referenced: linear ticket REDW-2048, GH PR runtime#542, internal eval set 'quant-regress-2027-12' (access: applied-ml drive)

Next meeting: 2027-12-15 09:00 UTC (30m) — target shorter agenda: status on current blockers + canary verdicts.
